title: When the Static Falls
premise: Petra Underhill smuggles memories—recorded lives, dead colonies, forbidden griefs—past orbital customs aboard the rusted freighter Kestrel's Wake. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, he wakes in the wrong body: a cryosleeping fleet officer named Ilsa Voss, whose consciousness was swapped into his during the anomaly. Trapped between the decaying colony of Meridian's Reach and a fleet truce about to expire, Petra must choose which half of humanity wakes first—while falling in love with the crew of misfits who become his family, and with the woman whose life he now carries in his head. In the end, Petra sacrifices his own identity to merge both memory-streams, waking both halves of humanity at once and dying as himself so that no one else has to be forgotten.
about_author: Freya Winterbourne is the pen name of a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the last broadcasts of abandoned research stations before turning to fiction. She writes science fiction about people history tried to lose, from a coastal town where the fog never quite lifts.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Aboard the Kestrel's Wake, Petra runs a shipment of illegal memory-chips past orbital customs, hiding them inside recordings of his own childhood on Meridian's Reach. We meet his found-family crew: gruff pilot Okafor, teenage engineer Junie, and medic Sable. The emotional beat is weary tenderness—Petra records everything because he cannot bear to let anything die unremembered.

chapters.title: The Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Gravity flickers across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; cargo floats, instruments scream, and Petra blacks out mid-sentence. He wakes in an unfamiliar body wearing a fleet uniform, in a cryo-bay he has never seen. The beat is vertigo and terror—the reader feels identity itself come loose.

chapters.title: I Am the Officer
chapters.summary: POV: Petra (in Ilsa Voss's body). Petra discovers he inhabits Fleet Lieutenant Ilsa Voss, thawed early by the anomaly, while somewhere his own body lies empty. Fleet AI interrogates him; he barely passes by drawing on Ilsa's leaked muscle-memory. Beat: impostor dread sharpened by grief—he can feel her loneliness like weather.

chapters.title: What the Colony Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Petra/Ilsa-body and Junie. The Kestrel's crew, believing Petra comatose, plays back his final recording and learns he suspected the anomaly was engineered. Meanwhile Petra, in Voss's body, finds her private logs: she voted to wake the fleet half first. Beat: betrayal and empathy entwined—her reasons are heartbreakingly human.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: POV: Petra (in Voss's body). The fleet council convenes; the truce protecting Meridian's Reach expires in six days, after which the colony's air rights revert to military use. Petra must argue the colony's case using only Voss's authority—and her voice. Beat: love against duty begins its real war; he defends a home that isn't his with a mouth that isn't either.

chapters.title: Junie's Signal
chapters.summary: POV: Junie. Junie decrypts Petra's hidden logs and finds coordinates for a black-market consciousness-bridge that could swap him back—but it requires both bodies awake simultaneously, something the fleet will never permit. She transmits a smuggler's handshake to Voss's terminal. Beat: fierce hope; the found family refuses to abandon their captain even as the fleet closes in.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Meridian
chapters.summary: POV: Petra (in Voss's body). Petra defects mid-mission, stealing a shuttle down to Meridian's Reach where the crew waits with the bridge rig. The reunion—his crew seeing their captain in a stranger's face—is raw and awkward and loving. Beat: belonging confirmed; identity revealed as something held by others, not just carried by oneself.

chapters.title: Two Streams
chapters.summary: POV: Petra, inside the bridge. The swap works partially: Petra returns to his own body but Ilsa's memories remain braided into his, and she wakes in hers with his. Through the shared stream they finally understand each other completely—and discover the anomaly was the colony's dying AI begging the fleet to remember it. Beat: intimacy as revelation; duty reframed as debt.

chapters.title: When the Static Falls
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. The fleet arrives to enforce the expired truce. Petra broadcasts the merged memory-stream—every recorded death, every forgotten day of Meridian's Reach—system-wide, forcing the entire fleet to experience the colony's slow dying in real time. Gravity flickers again as the AI spends its last strength holding the moment open. Beat: climax; grief weaponized into mercy.

chapters.title: Everyone Wakes
chapters.summary: POV: Ilsa, then ensemble. Shaken by nine seconds of shared memory, the fleet council ratifies a new accord: both halves of humanity wake together, and Meridian's Reach becomes the truce's memorial. Petra, burned out by carrying two lifetimes, fades gently among his crew—who record his final hours so that he, too, will be remembered. Beat: bittersweet resolution; love outlasting identity.
